title: Study in South Korea from Nepal: Your Complete Guide to GKS Scholarship & Tech Opportunities

children.text: Are you a Nepali student dreaming of a world-class education in one of Asia’s most dynamic countries? If so, studying in South Korea might be your perfect pathway to success. Moreover, with the prestigious GKS Scholarship and booming tech industry, South Korea offers unparalleled opportunities for ambitious students from Nepal.

In this comprehensive guide, we’ll walk you through everything you need to know about studying in South Korea, securing the coveted Korean Government Scholarship, and exploring exciting tech career prospects.
Why Study in South Korea from Nepal?
South Korea has emerged as a top destination for international students, particularly from Nepal. Here’s why:

Academic Excellence

First and foremost, South Korean universities consistently rank among the world’s best. Institutions like Seoul National University, KAIST, and Yonsei University offer cutting-edge programs in technology, engineering, and business. As a result, your degree will be recognized globally.

Affordable Education

Unlike Western countries, South Korea provides high-quality education at reasonable costs. Furthermore, numerous scholarship opportunities make it even more accessible for Nepali students.

Cultural Similarity

Additionally, Asian values and work ethics resonate well with Nepali culture. Consequently, adaptation becomes easier compared to Western countries.

Tech Innovation Hub

Most importantly, South Korea is home to global giants like Samsung, LG, and Hyundai. Therefore, students gain access to internships and career opportunities in leading technology companies.
Understanding the GKS Scholarship for Nepali Students

The Global Korea Scholarship (GKS), formerly known as KGSP, is a fully funded scholarship program of the Korean government, run by the National Institute for International Education (NIIED). It has separate undergraduate and graduate programs, each with its own guidelines and dates. The figures below come from the official NIIED 2027 undergraduate guidelines and the Korean Embassy in Nepal's 2026 graduate notice, checked in October 2026. Dates and amounts change every year, so always confirm on studyinkorea.go.kr.

Latest update for undergraduate applicants: the 2027 undergraduate (GKS-U) Embassy Track application window ran from September 15 to September 30, 2026 (Korea time) and has closed. First-round Embassy results are due by October 16. Applicants who do not pass can apply to the University Track, which runs from September to November 2026, with each university setting its own deadline.
What Does the GKS Scholarship Cover?
Benefits depend on the program. For the 2027 undergraduate program, NIIED lists:
Tuition: NIIED pays up to 5 million KRW per semester. The university covers any amount above that, plus the admission fee.
Korean language program fee: 5.2 million KRW per year.
Airfare: an economy class flight ticket (actual expense).

Monthly allowance: 13,560,000 KRW per year during the Korean language program and 14,400,000 KRW per year during the degree program, about 1,130,000 and 1,200,000 KRW a month. It is an all-inclusive subsidy for living expenses, accommodation, health insurance, Korean proficiency grants, the TOPIK application fee, the settlement allowance and degree completion grants.

NIIED says the scholarship amounts may change. The graduate program covers tuition, Korean language training fees, round-trip airfare and a monthly allowance. The 2026 Nepal notice does not state the allowance amount, so check the current notice.

How long the scholarship lasts: the undergraduate bachelor's track is 1 year of Korean language plus 4 to 6 years of degree study (5 to 7 years in total), and the associate degree track is 1 year of Korean plus 2 to 3 years (3 to 4 years in total). Applicants with TOPIK level 5 or 6 are exempt from the Korean language program. The graduate program is a 1-year Korean language program plus a 2-year master's or a 3-year doctoral program, or research of 6 months or 1 year.
GKS Scholarship Eligibility Criteria
Check the guideline for the program and the year you are applying to. These are the official criteria for the two programs most Nepali students ask about.
Undergraduate (GKS-U, 2027 intake)

Citizenship: you must hold citizenship of a country invited by NIIED (Nepal is). Your parents or legal guardians must hold citizenship of a country other than Korea. Applicants with dual Korean citizenship are not eligible.
Age: under 25 (born on or after March 1, 2002).

Education: for the bachelor's program, you graduated or are expected to graduate from high school or an associate degree program. For the associate degree program, from high school. Applicants who already hold a bachelor's degree cannot apply.

If you are expected to graduate, you must submit a certificate of expected graduation with your application, and your graduation certificate and transcript by December 31, 2026, or the acceptance is cancelled.

Grades: your CGPA from your previous program must meet one of three conditions: 80% or above on a 100-point scale, a rank within the top 20% of your class, or a CGPA of at least 2.64/4.0, 2.80/4.3, 2.91/4.5 or 3.23/5.0.
Health: you must be in good mental and physical health, with no grounds for disqualification for overseas travel, such as a criminal history.
Not eligible: graduates of Korean high schools or Korean associate programs, people who previously received a Korean government scholarship for a degree program, and former GKS degree scholars.
Graduate (GKS-G, 2026 Nepal notice)
Citizenship: Nepali.

Education: a bachelor's degree for the master's program, or a master's degree for the doctoral program, obtained by July 31 of the intake year. Expected graduates can apply but must submit their certificate and final transcript by that date.
Grades: 80% or above on a 100-point scale, or the top 20% of your class, or a GPA of at least 2.64/4.0, 2.80/4.3, 2.91/4.5 or 3.23/5.0.
Age: under 40 (born after September 1, 1986), or under 45 for professors.
Health: in good physical and mental health to study in Korea for the full program.
GKS Application Process: Step-by-Step Guide
Navigating the application process can seem overwhelming, but each step is clear once you know the order.
Step 1: Choose Your Application Track

For undergraduates, the Embassy Track is an online application at studyinkorea.go.kr, and it includes the General program and R-GKS, for regional universities. For 2027, Nepal has 2 Embassy Track places, 1 General and 1 R-GKS, out of 156 across 74 countries. The University Track means applying directly to a participating university under its own schedule, and it includes the UIC program (100 places at 13 universities, open to all countries) and the associate degree program. You can apply to only one program and one university. For graduates, the Korean Embassy in Nepal runs the Embassy Track, and candidates who do not pass can apply to the separate University Track.
Step 2: Prepare Required Documents
For the undergraduate Embassy Track, the guideline lists these documents:
Application form, personal statement, study plan and GKS applicant agreement, completed in the online system
One recommendation letter
Personal medical assessment and consent to collect and use personal information
Proof of citizenship of you and your parents, and proof of family relationship
High school graduation certificate (or certificate of expected graduation) and high school academic transcript, plus associate degree documents if you hold one
TOPIK score report or an English proficiency test score, if you have one
Optional: up to five copies of awards or other certificates
Your passport

Required certificates must be apostilled or consular confirmed, and documents in languages other than English or Korean need a certified translation. For graduate applicants in Nepal, all required certificates must be attested by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Government of Nepal, and translations also need that attestation.
Step 3: Submit Your Application

Submit during the application window. The 2027 undergraduate Embassy Track window was September 15 to September 30, 2026 (Korea time). The 2026 Nepal graduate window was February 12 to February 25, 2026 (Nepal time), which is only two weeks, so check the current notice early.
Step 4: Pass the Screening Process

Undergraduate selection has up to three rounds: the first by the embassy or university, the second by NIIED, and the third by your chosen university for Embassy Track applicants. In the 2027 cycle, the final announcement is expected on January 7, 2027. For Nepal's graduate program, only shortlisted candidates are invited to an interview, and certificates of successful candidates are consular confirmed by the Korean Embassy in Nepal.
Step 5: Accept Your Offer

Successful applicants confirm their university choice in the Study in Korea system by the deadline and prepare for departure. Check the results yourself on studyinkorea.go.kr, because NIIED does not inform applicants individually.
Pro Tip: Start early. The undergraduate Embassy Track window lasted only two weeks, and certificates need an apostille, consular confirmation or Foreign Ministry attestation.
Top Universities in South Korea for Nepali Students
When planning to study in South Korea from Nepal, choosing the right university is crucial. Here are the top institutions:
Seoul National University (SNU)
As Korea’s premier institution, SNU offers exceptional programs in engineering, natural sciences, and social sciences. Additionally, it provides strong support for international students.
Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology (KAIST)
Specifically designed for STEM students, KAIST offers world-class research facilities. Furthermore, all programs are taught in English, making it ideal for international students.
Yonsei University
One of Korea’s oldest universities, Yonsei combines traditional values with modern education. Similarly, it has a vibrant international community with students from over 100 countries.
Korea University
Known for its business and law programs, Korea University also excels in engineering and technology. Moreover, it has strong industry connections for internships.
Hanyang University
Particularly strong in engineering and technology, Hanyang University partners with leading Korean corporations. Therefore, students enjoy excellent job placement rates.
Tech Opportunities in South Korea for Nepali Students
Beyond education, South Korea offers incredible career prospects, especially in technology sectors.
Thriving Tech Industry
South Korea’s technology sector continues to grow exponentially. Consequently, demand for skilled professionals remains high. Key sectors include:
Software Development: AI, machine learning, and app development
Semiconductor Technology: Chip design and manufacturing
Robotics and Automation: Industrial and consumer robotics
5G and Telecommunications: Network infrastructure and development
E-commerce and Fintech: Digital payment systems and online platforms
Internship and Job Opportunities

International students can work part-time during their studies (up to 20 hours per week). Additionally, after graduation, students can apply for job-seeking visas (D-10) for up to 2 years. Visa and work rights change, so check the current rules with Korea Immigration at hikorea.go.kr.
Major companies actively recruit international talent:
Samsung Electronics
LG Group
SK Hynix
Kakao Corporation
Naver Corporation
Furthermore, South Korea’s startup ecosystem is booming, offering entrepreneurial opportunities for innovative minds.
Work Visa Pathways
After completing your studies, several visa options exist:
E-7 Visa: For specially designated activities (highly skilled workers)
D-10 Visa: Job-seeking visa for recent graduates
F-2 Visa: Points-based residence visa for long-term stay
As a result, many Nepali graduates successfully transition from student to professional life in Korea. Visa rules change, so check the current requirements at hikorea.go.kr.
Korean Language: Do You Need It?
While many programs are offered in English, learning Korean significantly enhances your experience. Here’s what you should know:

TOPIK (Test of Proficiency in Korean):

Although not always mandatory, TOPIK scores strengthen your application. Moreover, Level 3 or higher is typically required for Korean-taught programs.

Language Support:

Fortunately, most universities offer free Korean language courses. Additionally, the GKS scholarship includes a one-year Korean language program before the degree program. Undergraduate applicants with TOPIK level 5 or 6 are exempt.
Living in South Korea as a Nepali Student
Cost of Living
Monthly expenses typically range from 800,000 to 1,200,000 KRW (approximately NPR 80,000-120,000), including:
Accommodation: 300,000-500,000 KRW
Transportation: 60,000-100,000 KRW
Miscellaneous: 140,000-200,000 KRW
Importantly, the GKS scholarship covers most of these expenses.
Nepali Community
A growing Nepali community exists in major Korean cities. Therefore, you’ll find Nepali restaurants, cultural associations, and support networks. This makes the transition much smoother.
Safety and Quality of Life
South Korea ranks among the world’s safest countries. Furthermore, excellent public transportation, modern infrastructure, and high living standards ensure a comfortable student life.
Common Challenges and How to Overcome Them
Language Barrier
Solution: Utilize free language exchange programs and university Korean classes. Additionally, most Koreans are helpful to foreign students.
Cultural Adjustment
Solution: Join international student clubs and participate in cultural events. Moreover, maintain connections with the Nepali community for support.
Academic Pressure
Solution: Korean universities can be demanding. However, proper time management and utilizing the professor’s office hours help tremendously.
Application Timeline for Nepali Students
To successfully study in South Korea from Nepal, follow this timeline:
12 Months Before:
Research universities and programs
Prepare for language tests (TOPIK/IELTS)
Build your academic profile
8-10 Months Before:
Contact potential recommenders
Draft personal statements and study plans
Gather required documents
6 Months Before:
Check the current GKS notice: in recent cycles the undergraduate Embassy Track window was in September and the Nepal graduate window was in February.
Apply to universities directly (if doing University Track)
3-4 Months Before:
Prepare for interviews
Complete document verification
1-2 Months Before:
Apply for D-2 student visa
Arrange accommodation
Book flights

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: Can I work while studying in South Korea?

A: Yes, international students can work part-time up to 20 hours per week after completing six months of study. Check the current rules with Korea Immigration at hikorea.go.kr.

Q: How competitive is the GKS Scholarship?

A: For the 2027 undergraduate program, Nepal has 2 Embassy Track places (1 General and 1 R-GKS), out of 156 across 74 countries. The University Track has additional places, and the embassy may choose not to recommend a candidate. Strong grades and correctly certified documents matter most.

Q: Is IELTS mandatory for Korean universities?

A: For English-taught programs, yes. Most universities require IELTS 5.5-6.5 or equivalent TOEFL scores.

Q: Can I bring my family to South Korea?

A: Graduate students can apply for dependent visas for their spouse and children after arrival. Check the current rules with Korea Immigration at hikorea.go.kr.

Q: What are job prospects after graduation?

A: Excellent, especially in technology sectors. Many graduates secure positions in Korean multinational companies or return to Nepal with enhanced career prospects.
